headline: Decomposition breaks wholes into parts—sometimes destructively, sometimes productively
universal_truth: Everything complex can be broken down; understanding the parts helps you understand the whole
fun_facts: Decomposition of organic matter returns nutrients to soil—death feeds life
A car has about 30,000 parts—understanding requires decomposition into manageable pieces
Analysis literally means 'breaking apart' in Greek
discussion_questions: When has breaking something apart helped you understand it?
What complex problems could you decompose into smaller parts?
When is decomposition destructive versus productive?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Leaves fall and rot, returning nutrients to soil. Mechanics take apart engines to fix them. Scientists break down problems into components. Decomposition—coming apart—is everywhere, and it's often the path to understanding.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Breaking things down can be destructive or enlightening. What determines whether decomposition is helpful?

options.text: Decomposition is productive when it reveals how parts relate and enables either understanding or reconstruction—breaking down to build up
options.response: Yes. Productive decomposition breaks things into understandable pieces while tracking relationships. You take apart to learn, then reassemble with new insight.

options.text: Decomposition is always destructive—it breaks things
options.response: Sometimes, but strategic decomposition enables understanding and reconstruction...

q1.title: Analysis
q1.script: Analysis means breaking apart. Complex problems become manageable when decomposed. You can't hold everything in mind at once—decomposition lets you focus on pieces, then integrate understanding.

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Natural Decomposition
q2.script: In nature, decomposition recycles. Dead matter becomes nutrients for new life. Nothing is wasted; everything is repurposed. The end of one thing feeds the beginning of another.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Creative Destruction
q3.script: Sometimes you must take apart to rebuild better. Renovation demolishes before constructing. Editing cuts before polishing. Strategic destruction clears ground for improvement.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Everything complex can be broken down. Understanding the parts helps you understand the whole. Learn to decompose productively.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 232. Tomorrow, we'll explore using things again—recycling. Until then, pick a complex problem and break it into pieces.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Decomposition Practice - Break It Down
growTrack.activity: Take a complex problem or project you're facing. Break it into components—what are the parts? How do they relate? Often what seems overwhelming becomes manageable when decomposed into pieces you can address one at a time.
